findings.title: Dropper burns its lifetime airdrop budget even when the batch is refused
findings.problem: spawnAirdropMobs() is void and silently drops the whole batch on several early returns: dropLoc/mobType null, !isGameRunning(), or `toSpawn <= 0` when the mob cap is already full at the moment of arrival (WaveManager.java:982-989). executeAirdrop() increments airdropsDone unconditionally, so the per-dropper lifetime limit (airdrop-max-per-dropper, default 3, enforced only in shouldActivate() at line 73) is consumed by drops that spawned zero mobs. The cap check in shouldActivate() happens before the flight to the drop point, so the cap can fill during the ~1 s approach (DropperAttackGoal/other spawns), which is exactly when the refusal happens.
findings.impact: A flying-dropper that reaches its drop point while the arena is at the mob cap permanently stops airdropping after three such no-ops, even though it never produced a single airdrop mob. The wave still has to be cleared without those mobs; on crowded waves (global-mob-cap 80 / mob-cap-per-player 15) the dropper effectively becomes a plain harasser for the rest of its life.
findings.trigger: Wave spawns a flying-dropper; the active-mob count reaches the cap while it flies to its target (or a config sets airdrop-mob-type to null); AirdropSpawnGoal.tick() -> executeAirdrop() -> WaveManager.spawnAirdropMobs() returns at the `toSpawn <= 0` guard; airdropsDone is still incremented.

findings.title: shouldStayActive() does cross-world distanceSquared with no world guard
findings.problem: targetDropLocation is always built in gameManager.getGameWorld() (findDropLocation), but the dropper's current world is never compared to it. Bukkit Location#distanceSquared throws IllegalArgumentException when the two worlds differ. The sibling goal on the same entity documents and guards this exact hazard (DropperAttackGoal.findNearestPlayer, line 189-191: `if (dropperLoc.getWorld() != gameWorld) return null;` with the comment that cross-world distanceSquared throws), and DropperAttackGoal.tick()/isValidArenaTarget() also compare worlds before any distance call. AirdropSpawnGoal is the one path that does not.
findings.impact: As soon as the dropper is no longer in the arena world, every goal evaluation of that entity calls shouldStayActive() and throws IllegalArgumentException before the isValid()/isGameRunning() terms are reached, so the dropper does not cleanly deactivate — the failure surfaces as a repeated exception during the goal scheduler's evaluation of that mob for as long as it stays out of world with a pending drop target.
findings.trigger: An admin /tp's the flying-dropper out of the arena world (or any plugin teleports it) while it has a targetDropLocation; the next goal evaluation calls shouldStayActive() with a Location from another world.

findings.title: forceAdvanceWave completes the wave without cancelling the spawn batch or resetting waveSpawning
findings.problem: The RUNNING branch cancels the wave-check tick and calls onWaveComplete() immediately, but never cancels the in-flight spawn batch task (spawnTask, private to WaveManager) and never resets waveSpawning. checkWaveCompletion() deliberately gates on `!waveSpawning` (line 445) precisely so a half-finished batch cannot be judged cleared; the admin force path bypasses that gate, and onWaveComplete() flips the state to WAVE_INTERMISSION (only the last-wave branch reaches endGame, which does reset the flag at line 636). The still-scheduled BukkitRunnable fires up to 3 ticks later, sees state != RUNNING, calls cancelSpawnTask() and returns without running onComplete (the onComplete path at lines 164-169 is unreachable once the guard at 145 fires), so on the non-final-wave path waveSpawning is never reset by this call. Cancellation is therefore deferred by up to one batch period and depends entirely on the next task invocation rather than on the force-complete action.
findings.impact: On any wave short of the last one, waveSpawning stays true from the force-clear until the next wave's batch finishes, so the flag no longer means what checkWaveCompletion() assumes and the intermission runs with a stale "still spawning" state. Cancellation of the batch is also deferred by up to a full batch period (3 ticks) and depends on the task's own next invocation rather than on the force-complete action, so the arena declares the wave over while a spawn task is still live — exactly the window the M-12 guard exists to close.
findings.trigger: /hilltop wave clear (or any caller of GameManager#forceAdvanceWave) during GameState.RUNNING while WaveManager.spawnWave's 3-tick batch task is still running, i.e. in the first few seconds of a wave or on a large wave.

findings.title: Defeat settlement re-enters endGame(false) from the kick loop, double-ending the session
findings.problem: triggerDefeat() intentionally leaves GameState unchanged (ArenaInstance.triggerDefeat -> GameManager.haltGame only sets settlementPhase, so state is still RUNNING during the whole defeat countdown). When the countdown ends, ArenaInstance.finishSession() calls removePlayer() for each member, which reaches this min-players check while isGameRunning() is still true; removing enough players makes the check fire and calls endGame(false) a second time for the same lost game. endGame then re-broadcasts "game-defeat" to the remaining players, re-runs clearAllMobs()/deactivateSmash(), and invokes onGameEndCallback again (ArenaInstance.onNaturalGameEnd -> beginEndSequence is saved only by its isEnding() guard).
findings.impact: Players still in the arena at the end of the defeat countdown can receive a second "game-defeat" broadcast after the settlement screen already showed the result, and the natural-end callback runs twice for one session (the second beginEndSequence is suppressed only by its isEnding() guard). Any future side effect added to endGame() — stats, rewards, scoreboard refresh — would execute twice per lost game; today the damage is limited to the duplicate message and redundant teardown, hence low severity.
findings.trigger: Any defeat raised through ArenaInstance.triggerDefeat (e.g. defeat-all-down, defeat-villagers-dead), then the settlement countdown reaches 0 and finishSession() removes members so players.size() drops below the arena min-players while GameManager.state is still RUNNING.

unverified: GameManager.checkWaveCompletion (line 425-437) cancels its own waveCheckTask even when liveArena() returns null, so no defeat is triggered and no further wave checks happen; I could not find a reachable main-thread path where a running arena is absent from MultiArenaManager, so this is not reported.

WaveManager.spawnAirdropMobs (line 1011) calls world.spawnEntity without a try/catch; a configured but unspawnable EntityType (e.g. PLAYER) would let the exception escape the repeating task, cancelling it and leaving its handle in airdropTasks forever. Not reported because it needs an invalid-but-parseable airdrop-mob-type value.
notes: WaveManager accounting reviewed in depth: activeMobs is a concurrent identity set, isWaveCleared() prunes invalid entities every check, discardMob/purgeStuckMobs/relocateStuckMobsToPlayers all remove from the set, clearAllMobs cancels both spawnTask and airdropTasks before removing entities, and the three spawn paths share the same `state != RUNNING` self-cancel guard; I found no orphan/off-by-one defect there beyond S06-F3. PlayerGoodsManager reviewed for save/restore ordering and async-vs-main races: snapshot is put before the inventory is cleared, restore applies everything before removing the entry (retryable on exception), every write allocates a monotonic seq on the main thread and writeYaml re-checks it before serialization and before the atomic move, unique tmp names prevent interleaved writes, and scheduleSaveToDisk falls back to a synchronous saveNow() when the plugin is disabled, so no lost-update or double-restore path was found. GameManager's victory short-circuit, cancelWaveScheduler coverage on all stop paths, and the 3 s wave-check lifecycle also look correct; the defects above are the residual issues. PlayerData is a plain main-thread counter holder with no synchronization hazard observed.
